section_summary: This section closes a 1942 British publication listing Japanese ships and aircraft destroyed or damaged by Netherlands forces, then turns to 1943 U.S. diplomatic reporting on Japanese propaganda in occupied Indonesia. A State Department note, Walter A. Foote’s despatch, and an enclosed memorandum by Ch. O. van der Plas describe declining Indonesian confidence in an Allied return, the collaboration or coerced cooperation of prominent nationalist leaders, and proposals for tropical-band broadcasts and leaflet drops coordinated with military action.

subfiles.title: Japanese Ships and Planes Destroyed or Damaged by the Netherlands Fighting Forces up to January 26, 1942
subfiles.about: The pamphlet lists Japanese ships and aircraft reported destroyed or damaged by Netherlands forces during December 1941 and January 1942.
subfiles.summary: Pamphlet crediting Netherlands forces with sinking or damaging many Japanese ships and shooting down ten aircraft up to January 26, 1942.

subfiles.title: Department of State Note on Despatch No. 25, “Propaganda Directed Towards the Netherlands Indies”
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, U.S. Department of State
subfiles.about: The note summarizes and recommends reading the Batavia consul general’s despatch concerning Japanese and Allied propaganda in occupied Indonesia.
subfiles.summary: Note on Despatch No. 25: Indonesian leaders, doubting early Allied return, grow inclined to cooperate with Japan; broadcasts and leaflets over Java were proposed, but need military support.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 25: Propaganda Directed Towards the Netherlands Indies
subfiles.from: Walter A. Foote, American Consul General at Batavia, temporarily at Melbourne
subfiles.about: Foote transmits van der Plas’s memorandum and assesses why Japanese propaganda was becoming more effective among Indonesians.
subfiles.summary: Foote says distorted Allied statements and no major offensive weakened Indonesian confidence and encouraged Sukarno and others to cooperate with Japan; tropical-wave broadcasts and leaflets would fail without sustained military action.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Japanese Propaganda and Psychological Warfare in the Netherlands Indies
subfiles.about: The memorandum examines Japanese intimidation and propaganda, the involvement of Indonesian leaders in occupation institutions, and possible Allied countermeasures.
subfiles.summary: Van der Plas says Japanese propaganda sought to persuade Indonesians Allied recovery was impossible; leaders' cooperation reflects coercion or despair, and he recommends tropical-band broadcasts and leaflets over Java.
